---
title: "TERRE GRS: Epigenome-wide asssociation analysis"
output: html_notebook
---

The manuscript "A Parkinson’s disease genetic risk score associates with blood DNAm on chromosome 17" explores how a genetic risk score (GRS) for Parkinson's disease (PD) associates with blood DNA methylation in the TERRE study of French agricultural workers, and evaluates GRS associations with DNAm in each sex as well as their sensitivity to non-genetic factors. This was originally spearheaded by Will Casazza and was posted as a pre-print on medRxiv in 2023. The current revision (2024, led by Sam Schaffner) aims to address previous reviewer feedback and prepare the manuscript for re-submission.


In this script, EWAS is conducted to identify DNAm patterns associated with the GRS in the cross-sex and sex-stratified samples in TERRE. The models are adjusted for batch, cell type, and disease status. Results will be compared with the previous models (adjusted for 10 DNAm PCs).


Last updated Mar 20, 2026 by Samantha Schaffner: Controlling for pesticide exposure.

Based on code by Will Casazza

# Association analysis

## EWAS model checks

Prior to looking at results, I'll assess whether the new EWAS model seems appropriate using three measures:

*1. Variance inflation factor*: The variance inflation factor (VIF) can be used to detect collinearity. Higher VIF values indicate a greater degree of collinearity. Typically VIF < 5 is considered acceptable.


*2. Q-Q plot of nominal p-values*: If the variable of interest does not affect global DNAm, p-values should distribute close to the center line on a normal Q-Q plot, with some deviation at the tail indicating associations detected. The shape of the Q-Q plot can visually indicate model inflation or deflation.


*3. Bias and inflation calculations*: The "bacon" package (van Iterson et al., 2017) was developed to calculate and optionally, correct for, bias and inflation observed in epigenome-wide association studies. It models test statistics using a Bayesian mixture model, and estimates the model parameters: bias (mean) and inflation (standard deviation). The Bayesian mixture model is proposed to more accurately model the quantitative nature and technical/biological influences on epigenomic and transcriptomic data, as opposed to the traditional genomic inflation factor (based on discrete genotypes).


```{r ewas models, eval=F}
## Preparing data
# match meta data and M-values
meta <- meta[complete.cases(meta$CTP_PC1),]
mvals <- mvals[,match(meta$patient, colnames(mvals))]
all(colnames(mvals)==meta$patient) #TRUE

# subset meta data to relevant columns and re-format
meta_sub <- meta[,c("patient","GRS_scaled","SCORE1_AVG","PD","age","sex","geno_V3","geno_V4","geno_V5","CTP_PC1","CTP_PC2","CTP_PC3","CTP_PC4","CTP_PC5","CTP_PC6","smoking","pesticides","head_trauma","alcohol1","levodopa","agonist","plate","SentrixPosition_A")]
str(meta_sub)
meta_sub$PD <- as.factor(meta_sub$PD)
meta_sub$sex <- as.factor(meta_sub$sex)
meta_sub$smoking <- as.factor(meta_sub$smoking)
meta_sub$pesticides <- as.factor(meta_sub$pesticides)
meta_sub$head_trauma <- as.factor(meta_sub$head_trauma)
meta_sub$alcohol1 <- as.factor(meta_sub$alcohol1)
meta_sub$levodopa <- as.factor(meta_sub$levodopa)
meta_sub$plate <- as.factor(meta_sub$plate)
meta_sub$SentrixPosition_A <- as.factor(meta_sub$SentrixPosition_A)

## Variance inflation factor
# check for one CpG (result is the same as when applied to all CpGs and averaged)
vif(lm(mvals[1,] ~ meta_sub$GRS_scaled + meta_sub$age + meta_sub$sex + meta_sub$geno_V3 + meta_sub$geno_V4 + meta_sub$geno_V5 + meta_sub$CTP_PC1 + meta_sub$CTP_PC2 + meta_sub$CTP_PC3 + meta_sub$CTP_PC4 + meta_sub$CTP_PC5 + meta_sub$CTP_PC6 + meta_sub$plate + meta_sub$SentrixPosition_A + meta_sub$PD))[,3]
#       meta_sub$GRS_scaled               meta_sub$age               meta_sub$sex           meta_sub$geno_V3 
#                  1.065854                   1.106000                   1.546047                   1.087091 
#          meta_sub$geno_V4           meta_sub$geno_V5           meta_sub$CTP_PC1           meta_sub$CTP_PC2 
#                  1.101140                   1.060779                   1.096934                   1.131434 
#          meta_sub$CTP_PC3           meta_sub$CTP_PC4           meta_sub$CTP_PC5           meta_sub$CTP_PC6 
#                  1.322629                   1.142134                   1.251003                   1.159699 
#            meta_sub$plate meta_sub$SentrixPosition_A                meta_sub$PD 
#                  1.135932                   1.051763                   1.066487 


## Q-Q plot
#scaled GRS
pvals <- sapply(1:nrow(mvals), function(x) {
  coef(summary(lm(mvals[x,] ~ meta_sub$GRS_scaled + meta_sub$age + meta_sub$sex + meta_sub$geno_V3 + meta_sub$geno_V4 + meta_sub$geno_V5 + meta_sub$CTP_PC1 + meta_sub$CTP_PC2 + meta_sub$CTP_PC3 + meta_sub$CTP_PC4 + meta_sub$CTP_PC5 + meta_sub$CTP_PC6 + meta_sub$plate + meta_sub$SentrixPosition_A + meta_sub$PD)))[2,4]
   }) #runtime ~1 hour
qqunif.plot(pvals, title="Model adjusted for PD, batch, and cell type")

## Bias and inflation (based on Z-values)
zvals <- qnorm(pvals)
bacon(zvals)
#...estimated bias: -0.092.
#...estimated inflation: 0.99.

## Model without adjustment for PD
## Q-Q plot
#scaled GRS
pvals <- sapply(1:nrow(mvals), function(x) {
  coef(summary(lm(mvals[x,] ~ meta_sub$GRS_scaled + meta_sub$age + meta_sub$sex + meta_sub$geno_V3 + meta_sub$geno_V4 + meta_sub$geno_V5 + meta_sub$CTP_PC1 + meta_sub$CTP_PC2 + meta_sub$CTP_PC3 + meta_sub$CTP_PC4 + meta_sub$CTP_PC5 + meta_sub$CTP_PC6 + meta_sub$plate + meta_sub$SentrixPosition_A)))[2,4]
   }) #runtime ~1 hour
qqunif.plot(pvals, title="Model adjusted for batch, and cell type")

## Bias and inflation (based on Z-values)
zvals <- qnorm(pvals)
bacon(zvals)
#...estimated bias: -0.13.
#...estimated inflation: 1.
```

## Meta data correlation heat map
```{r meta heat, eval=F}
source("~/kobor_shared_coding_resource/PCA_Plot_Function.R")
source("~/kobor_shared_coding_resource/correlation_pval.R")

#Create correlation matrix
terre_meta_cor <- meta_sub[,-(c(1,3))] #remove "patient" and non-scaled GRS
cormat <- correlation_pval(terre_meta_cor)

# Get lower triangle of the correlation matrix
get_lower_tri<-function(cormat){
    cormat[upper.tri(cormat)] <- NA
    return(cormat)
  }
# Get upper triangle of the correlation matrix
get_upper_tri <- function(cormat){
    cormat[lower.tri(cormat)]<- NA
    return(cormat)
  }

upper_tri <- get_upper_tri(cormat)

#colour if sig
for(x in 1:nrow(upper_tri)){
  for(y in 1:ncol(upper_tri)){
    if(is.na(upper_tri[x,y])==FALSE){
    if(as.numeric(upper_tri[x,y])<=0.001){upper_tri[x,y]<-"<=0.001"}else{
    if(as.numeric(upper_tri[x,y])<=0.01){upper_tri[x,y]<-"<=0.01"}else{
      if(as.numeric(upper_tri[x,y])<=0.05){upper_tri[x,y]<-"<=0.05"}else{upper_tri[x,y]<-">0.05"}}}}
  }}
melted_cormat <- reshape2::melt(upper_tri, na.rm = TRUE)
png("~/PD_GRS/EWAS_TERRE/terre_meta_cor_1Feb2026.png", width=600, height=600)
ggplot(data = melted_cormat, aes(Var2, Var1, fill = value))+
 geom_tile(color = "white")+
scale_fill_manual(values=c("#084594","#4292c6","#9ecae1","#deebf7"), name="p-value") +
  theme_minimal()+ 
 theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, vjust = 1, 
    size = 12, hjust = 1))+
 coord_fixed()
dev.off()
```
![Meta data correlation heat map](/home1/NEURO/schaffner/PD_GRS/EWAS_TERRE/terre_meta_cor_1Feb2026.png)

Sex is correlated strongly with cell type, smoking, pesticide exposure, and alcohol intake.

Row is correlated strongly with cell type PC5.

The GRS correlates moderately with PD status.

## Sex stratification

While there is not expected to be a strong "tail" on the Q-Q plot due to lack of association between the GRS and DNAm PCs, let's aim to reduce the model bias and see if any associations are detectable. As males and females have very different exposure levels, we will start by sex-stratifying the data.


## Cross-sex model adjusted for environmental covariates

Finally, let's go back to the cross-sex model and see how this looks when adjusted for head trauma, smoking, alcohol, and pesticide exposure.

```{r terre cross sex cov adj, eval=F}
#scaled GRS
pvals_x_sex <- sapply(1:nrow(mvals), function(x) {
  coef(summary(lm(mvals[x,] ~ meta_sub$GRS_scaled + meta_sub$age + meta_sub$sex + meta_sub$geno_V3 + meta_sub$geno_V4 + meta_sub$geno_V5 + meta_sub$CTP_PC1 + meta_sub$CTP_PC2 + meta_sub$CTP_PC3 + meta_sub$CTP_PC4 + meta_sub$CTP_PC5 + meta_sub$CTP_PC6 + meta_sub$plate + meta_sub$SentrixPosition_A + meta_sub$PD + meta_sub$head_trauma + meta_sub$smoking + meta_sub$alcohol1 + meta_sub$pesticides)))[2,4]
   })
png("~/PD_GRS/EWAS_TERRE/qqplot_ht_smoke_alc_pest.png")
qqunif.plot(pvals_x_sex, title="Model adjusted for head trauma, smoking, alcohol, and pesticides")
dev.off()

## Bias and inflation (based on Z-values)
zvals <- qnorm(pvals_x_sex)
bacon(zvals)
#Bacon-object containing 1 set(s) of 803777 test-statistics.
#...estimated bias: -0.075.
#...estimated inflation: 0.91.
```
![Q-Q plot for covariate-adjusted cross-sex EWAS model](/home1/NEURO/schaffner/PD_GRS/EWAS_TERRE/qqplot_ht_smoke_alc_pest.png)

There is a minor improvement in the cross-sex model adjusted for additional covariates, though it is quite similar overall to the unadjusted model.


## Differential methylation analysis

Will used limma on all EPIC probes passing QC, modeling the data with M-values. I'll continue with this approach and transform results back to beta values later for plotting and interpretation purposes.

First, as Will did, I'll apply the updated models to (1) the cross-sex sample, (2) males, (3) females, (4) PD cases, and (5) controls. This permits us to detect whether GRS associations with DNAm are dependent on sex and/or disease status.

```{r prs ewas, eval=F}
####### Cross-sex PRS EWAS
# limma design matrix and linear model fit
design_prs <- model.matrix(~ 1 + GRS_scaled + age + sex + geno_V3 + geno_V4 + geno_V5 + CTP_PC1 + CTP_PC2 + CTP_PC3 + CTP_PC4 + CTP_PC5 + CTP_PC6 + plate + SentrixPosition_A + PD, data = meta_sub)
prs_fit <- lmFit(mvals, design_prs)
prs_fit <- eBayes(prs_fit)
# transform adjusted M-values to adjusted beta-values (code from Kruppa et al. 2021)
prs_fit_coef <- prs_fit$coefficients
m0_eff <- prs_fit_coef[, "(Intercept)"] #M-value model intercept
m1_eff <- m0_eff + prs_fit_coef[, "GRS_scaled"] #M-value model intercept plus GRS coefficient (delta M)

prs_res <- limma::topTable(prs_fit, coef = 2, number = Inf, genelist=rownames(mvals))
prs_res$adjDB <- m2beta(m1_eff) - m2beta(m0_eff) #transform each adjusted M-value to a beta-value, and subtract intercept beta value from intercept + coefficient beta value to obtain the adjusted delta beta
nrow(prs_res[abs(prs_res$adjDB)>=0.03 & prs_res$adj.P.Val<=0.05,]) #0
#### logFC column is the model coefficient

# limma design matrix and linear model fit: no PD
design_prs_nopd <- model.matrix(~ 1 + GRS_scaled + age + sex + geno_V3 + geno_V4 + geno_V5 + CTP_PC1 + CTP_PC2 + CTP_PC3 + CTP_PC4 + CTP_PC5 + CTP_PC6 + plate + SentrixPosition_A, data = meta_sub)
prs_fit_nopd <- lmFit(mvals, design_prs_nopd)
prs_fit_nopd <- eBayes(prs_fit_nopd)
# transform adjusted M-values to adjusted beta-values (code from Kruppa et al. 2021)
prs_fit_nopd_coef <- prs_fit_nopd$coefficients
m0_eff <- prs_fit_nopd_coef[, "(Intercept)"] #M-value model intercept
m1_eff <- m0_eff + prs_fit_nopd_coef[, "GRS_scaled"] #M-value model intercept plus GRS coefficient (delta M)

prs_res_nopd <- limma::topTable(prs_fit_nopd, coef = 2, number = Inf, genelist=rownames(mvals))
prs_res_nopd$adjDB <- m2beta(m1_eff) - m2beta(m0_eff) #transform each adjusted M-value to a beta-value, and subtract intercept beta value from intercept + coefficient beta value to obtain the adjusted delta beta
nrow(prs_res_nopd[abs(prs_res_nopd$adjDB)>=0.03 & prs_res_nopd$adj.P.Val<=0.05,]) #0

####### Cases only
design_prs_case <- model.matrix(~ 1 + GRS_scaled + age + sex + geno_V3 + geno_V4 + geno_V5 + CTP_PC1 + CTP_PC2 + CTP_PC3 + CTP_PC4 + CTP_PC5 + CTP_PC6 + plate + SentrixPosition_A, data = meta_sub[meta_sub$PD=="1",])
prs_fit_case <- lmFit(mvals[,match(unlist(meta_sub[meta_sub$PD=="1","patient"]), colnames(mvals))], design_prs_case)
prs_fit_case <- eBayes(prs_fit_case)
# transform adjusted M-values to adjusted beta-values (code from Kruppa et al. 2021)
prs_fit_coef <- prs_fit_case$coefficients
m0_eff <- prs_fit_coef[, "(Intercept)"] #M-value model intercept
m1_eff <- m0_eff + prs_fit_coef[, "GRS_scaled"] #M-value model intercept plus GRS coefficient (delta M)

case_res <- limma::topTable(prs_fit_case, coef = 2, number = Inf, genelist=rownames(mvals))
case_res$adjDB <- m2beta(m1_eff) - m2beta(m0_eff) #transform each adjusted M-value to a beta-value, and subtract intercept beta value from intercept + coefficient beta value to obtain the adjusted delta beta
nrow(case_res[abs(case_res$adjDB)>=0.03 & case_res$adj.P.Val<=0.05,]) #0

# Controls only
design_prs_control <- model.matrix(~ 1 + GRS_scaled + age + sex + geno_V3 + geno_V4 + geno_V5 + CTP_PC1 + CTP_PC2 + CTP_PC3 + CTP_PC4 + CTP_PC5 + CTP_PC6 + plate + SentrixPosition_A, data = meta_sub[meta_sub$PD=="0",])

# Males

nrow(male_res[abs(male_res$adjDB)>=0.03 & male_res$adj.P.Val<=0.05,]) #0

# Females
design_prs_female <- model.matrix(~ 1 + GRS_scaled + age + geno_V3 + geno_V4 + geno_V5 + CTP_PC1 + CTP_PC2 + CTP_PC3 + CTP_PC4 + CTP_PC5 + CTP_PC6 + plate + SentrixPosition_A + PD, data = meta_F)
prs_fit_female <- lmFit(mvals[,match(unlist(meta_F[,"patient"]), colnames(mvals_F))], design_prs_female)
prs_fit_female <- eBayes(prs_fit_female)
# transform adjusted M-values to adjusted beta-values (code from Kruppa et al. 2021)
prs_fit_coef <- prs_fit_female$coefficients
m0_eff <- prs_fit_coef[, "(Intercept)"] #M-value model intercept

female_res <- limma::topTable(prs_fit_female, coef = 2, number = Inf, genelist=rownames(mvals))

# PD status EWAS check
design_pd <- model.matrix(~ 1 + PD + age + sex + geno_V3 + geno_V4 + geno_V5 + CTP_PC1 + CTP_PC2 + CTP_PC3 + CTP_PC4 + CTP_PC5 + CTP_PC6 + plate + SentrixPosition_A, data = meta_sub)
pd_fit <- lmFit(mvals, design_pd)
pd_fit <- eBayes(pd_fit)
# transform adjusted M-values to adjusted beta-values (code from Kruppa et al. 2021)
```

```{r prs ewas no cov, eval=F}

####### Cross-sex PRS EWAS

# transform adjusted M-values to adjusted beta-values (code from Kruppa et al. 2021)
prs_fit_coef_nopd <- prs_fit_nopd$coefficients
m0_eff <- prs_fit_coef_nopd[, "(Intercept)"] #M-value model intercept
m1_eff <- m0_eff + prs_fit_coef_nopd[, "GRS_scaled"] #M-value model intercept plus GRS coefficient (delta M)

prs_res_nopd <- limma::topTable(prs_fit_nopd, coef = 2, number = Inf, genelist=rownames(mvals_sub))
prs_res_nopd$adjDB <- m2beta(m1_eff) - m2beta(m0_eff) #transform each adjusted M-value to a beta-value, and subtract intercept beta value from intercept + coefficient beta value to obtain the adjusted delta beta
nrow(prs_res_nopd[abs(prs_res_nopd$adjDB)>=0.03 & prs_res_nopd$adj.P.Val<=0.05,]) #0
#### logFC column is the model coefficient

#Volcano plot: M-values
colnames(prs_res_nopd)[2:3] <- c("delta_M", "avgM")
summary(prs_res_nopd$threshold_M <- (prs_res_nopd$adj.P.Val <= 0.05 & abs(prs_res_nopd$delta_M)>=1.5)) #0
prs_res_nopd$DNAm_change <- "NS"

max(abs(prs_res_nopd$delta_M)) #0.7176475
max(-log10(prs_res_nopd$P.Value)) #6.362772

png("~/PD_GRS/EWAS_TERRE/volcano_GRS_Mvals_env_noPD_20Mar26.png", width=200, height=250)
ggplot(prs_res_nopd[,c("delta_M","P.Value","DNAm_change")], aes(x=delta_M, y=-log10(P.Value), colour=DNAm_change)) +
  geom_point(size=1.75) +
  xlab("Adjusted Delta M") + ylab("-log10 P-Value") + theme_classic() + scale_color_manual(values=c("gray70")) + geom_hline(yintercept=-log10(9e-07)) + geom_vline(xintercept=-1.5) + geom_vline(xintercept=1.5) + ylim(c(0,10)) + xlim(c(-1.8,1.8)) + theme(legend.position="none")
dev.off()

####### Cases only
design_prs_case <- model.matrix(~ 1 + GRS_scaled + age + sex + geno_V3 + geno_V4 + geno_V5 + CTP_PC1 + CTP_PC2 + CTP_PC3 + CTP_PC4 + CTP_PC5 + CTP_PC6 + plate + SentrixPosition_A + head_trauma + smoking + alcohol1 + pesticides, data = meta_pest[meta_pest$PD=="1",])
prs_fit_case <- lmFit(mvals_sub[,match(unlist(meta_pest[meta_pest$PD=="1","patient"]), colnames(mvals_sub))], design_prs_case)
prs_fit_case <- eBayes(prs_fit_case)

nrow(case_res[abs(case_res$adjDB)>=0.03 & case_res$adj.P.Val<=0.05,]) #0
```

## Summary and next steps

No models, regardless of sex or disease stratification, had any CpGs passing M-value and adjusted p-value cutoffs. This suggested the SNPs in the GRS had little influence on DNAm compared with sex and exposures, which were correlated with DNAm PCs.


Sample breakdown:

218 total

71 PD cases

147 controls

100 females

118 males
